newsitem.title: UK: UK's SFA confirms SBC Warburg probe.
newsitem.headline: UK's SFA confirms SBC Warburg probe.

text.p: Britain's Securities and Futures Authority on Wednesday confirmed it is investigating SBC Warburg, the investment banking arm of Swiss Bank Corp, in a probe said by banking sources to concern the sale of shares on behalf of an investment trust last year.
"I can confirm that SFA is formally investigating SBC Warburg," the SFA spokesman said, adding he could make no further comment at this stage.
The investigation is into the alleged mishandling of the sale of 300 million pounds ($478 million) of European shares for an investment trust, banking sources said.

They said the SFA investigation centred on the sharp fall of several European share prices in October, after SBC Warburg carried out a series of share sales for Kleinwort European Privatisation Investment Trust(KEPIT).
The sources said there had been an internal review at SBC Warburg and internal disciplinary action had been carried out. One executive recently left the company as a result.

The Financial Times said on Wednesday the share sale was believed to have resulted in a "multi-million pound" loss but banking sources said the figure was not that high and noted that SBC had made no provision for an extraordinary trading loss in its accounts published today. ($ = 0.627 British Pounds)
